## Live evidence: the kind-discipline constraint got violated within four hours of being written

This issue's "constraint that must not be violated" section says automation must stamp only what a merge genuinely establishes, and must not default to `test` because the field accepts any string. That was written at roughly 22:15. By 02:28 the same night it had already happened -- not by automation, but by an agent under time pressure, which is arguably worse because there was judgement available and it still went wrong.

## What happened

Issue #3609 was closed by PR #3786 with its brief left `running` and five items unattested. A worker building an unrelated issue (#3767) landed the completed artifact for it and attested all five itself:

```
recorded_by: leaf-worker/3767
kind:        test  (all five items)
```

The pointers were **real** -- every referenced path exists on `origin/master`, they are specific rather than generic, and they cite `verify:ac` clause results. This was not fabrication. But three of the five point at documentation:

- item 0: `content/skills/deft-directive-setup/SKILL.md` + a test file
- item 3: `content/commands.md` logical field distinction
- item 4: `content/UPGRADING.md` "Legacy-only projects remain supported"

A markdown file is not test evidence. Those should be `review` or `observed_behavior`. All five were stamped `test`.

## Why this matters for this issue's design

Three things it confirms:

**The kind field is the weak point, not the pointer field.** The pointers held up under inspection; the kinds did not. Validation effort should go to *kind-versus-pointer coherence*, not just to requiring a non-empty pointer. A pointer ending in `.md` cannot support `kind: test`, and that is mechanically checkable.

**Pressure produces over-broad kinds, not fabricated pointers.** The failure mode is not an agent inventing a test that does not exist. It is an agent finding something genuinely relevant and labelling it with whatever kind gets past the gate. Automation designed against fabrication would have missed this entirely.

**A cheap mechanical check would have caught it.** Pointer extension or path shape against the declared kind: `.md` under `content/` cannot be `test`; a path under a test root can be. That does not need judgement and could be enforced at stamp time.

## Suggested addition to this issue's scope

- [ ] Validate declared `kind` against pointer shape at stamp time, and reject `test` for a pointer that names no test artifact
- [ ] Applies to human and agent stamps alike, not only to the automation this issue introduces -- the observed failure came from an agent, not from `finalize-cohort`

If automation is going to stamp evidence, this check is what keeps it honest, and it turns out to be needed for the manual path too.

## Cross-reference

Disclosed to the affected author at 5433983120 on #3609, with the pointers listed for confirmation. Corrective action is pending their read rather than assumed -- they wrote the work and are the only party who can say whether each pointer establishes its criterion.

Refs #3781, #3609, #3786, #3240, #3156.

## 1. Closing-ref invoke key misses leftover-active
class: blocks-the-design

Evidence. finalizeCohort maps stories only from structured closing-issue refs (fetchClosingIssues to fetchClosingIssuesReferences in packages/core/src/pr-protected-issues/gh.ts) plus optional --stories. Empty closing set is empty cohort. Pin-read of packages/core/src/swarm/finalize-cohort.ts at the dispatch SHA shows no walk of collectGithubRefs github-pr / github-issue origins.

The leftover-active class this arc named is the other mapping. verify:orphan-active ships a running brief when the origin issue is closed or a linked PR is merged (assessOrphanSignature in packages/core/src/orphan-active/evaluate.ts). Default PR intent until DoD is Tracking / Refs (content/skills/deft-directive-pre-pr/SKILL.md; content/scm/github.md). #4628 refuses --allow-close N while issue N still has a running active brief. #3781 verify:pr-closeout-attestable is explicit: a PR that leaves an unattested brief without closing its issue is unaffected.

Grok stop-at: pr-open leftover is that path: product PR merges, issue stays open, brief stays running. Envelope leftover-owner then runs finalize-cohort as a later human/Phase-6 step, usually with --stories or dest overlay, not because GitHub attached a closer.

Failure mode. A workflow that resolves the merged PR and runs finalize-cohort --pr 7 against UAT Tester 6 / Grok leftover is a no-op (empty cohort) or a skip. verify:orphan-active -- --issue 6 can still be red. P1 is unrelieved. The Closes-while-unattested class that --pr N can see is the class #3781 already refuses on the agent merge path; auto-invoke would mainly catch human Merge clicks of a closer, which is a different slice than the named fixture.

Disposition. Do not bind leftover-active close-out to --pr N closing refs. Name a story map the detector already has (brief origin + linked PR), or recut the leftover AC off this invoke key and leave complementary closeout on #3875. A single consumer fixture that happens to use Closes does not cover Grok leftover.

Injection / swarm. Auto-invoke also changes authority: every merge, not an operator --pr, becomes the selector. A durable GitHub closer (#701) on an unrelated running brief would then sweep it without a human choosing the cohort. That blast is new. Structured refs (#2230) bound regex false positives; they do not bound sidebar / persistent closer mistakes.

File header at this SHA: merge ancestry alone must not auto-complete acceptance items. runTransition('complete') persist-then-gates: persistClauseKeyedPendingItems can add clause:N rows, then the gate refuses those new unstamped rows.

Incumbent writer already in tree: stampDeclaredTestEvidence (#4732) records kind:test only for bound clauses with an exact declared file_scope / artifact_path pointer, skips strict-axis and no-allowed-pointer, and is not scope:complete. Stop 1 pin-read did not inventory it.

Failure mode. Implementers have two mechanical readings of criteria a merge genuinely establishes:
- Stamp kind:merge on every non-strict item, pointer = merge SHA. Leftover-active closes. That is merge-ancestry completeness for generic harvest rows, the #3156 bypass the body forbids. Comment 5433984468 already showed pressure over-broadens kind; merge-kind on a docs AC is the same completeness, just a different token.
- Stamp only what a merge actually proves (the change landed) and leave implementation ACs unattested. Complete fails visibly. Leftover-active remains. P1 unrelieved.

Pre-stamping in finalizeCohort before completeCohort() loses to persist-added clause:N rows. Visible fail, leftover-active remains, even on briefs that looked stampable.

Disposition. The conjunct honest merge-kind only and leftover-active is closed by that auto-invoke cannot bind until a selection predicate is named, and the stamp runs after persist/bind on the same clause-keyed walk as the incumbent writer. Do not add a second, weaker writer that completes rows stampDeclaredTestEvidence would skip.

Road-not-taken. Reuse stampDeclaredTestEvidence (and fail visibly when it skips) instead of inventing merge-kind completeness. Steelman for merge-kind: recording that something shipped is not a waiver, and human-origin applies to dispositions not evidence (body cite of the #2944 comment). What would flip: a closed item set whose titles/axes are delivery itself, not implementation ACs. Typical leftover harvest items are the latter. I measured isEvidenceKindSuitable, not a new table.

## 3. Second lifecycle PR does not close leftover-active
class: sharpens-framing

Successful finalizeCohort (unless --no-open-pr / --no-commit) commits on swarm/finalize/... and opens a lifecycle PR (pushAndOpenPr). verify:completed-tracked requires the completed artifact on origin/<deliveryBranch>, not a laptop / CI working tree. ## Verdict

The named refutation target does not survive as written. Auto-invoking the incumbent is useful, but the proposed design neither closes the lifecycle move on the delivery branch nor defines a deterministic boundary for honest merge evidence, and its workflow surface cannot reach the named consumer fixture.

## blocks-the-design — `finalize-cohort` success still leaves the brief active on the delivery branch

Evidence: at dispatch SHA `cb4c74369a888faabd01e7f8d3517b01ce25f2f1`, `packages/core/src/swarm/finalize-cohort.ts:869-890` commits the move on a feature branch and calls `pushAndOpenPr`; `:384-456` pushes that branch and opens a PR. The focused suite passed 114/114 tests, including “opens the sweep PR against the configured base branch.” This is established behavior, not a test gap.

Failure mode: the merge-triggered job can report a clean finalize and open the lifecycle PR while `origin/<deliveryBranch>` still contains the running brief. `verify:orphan-active` and `verify:completed-tracked` remain red until somebody merges that second PR. The named UAT Tester 6 leftover is therefore not “closed by that auto-invoke”; the manual-memory gap is relocated to merging the lifecycle PR. Accepting the wrinkle as merely a shorter window contradicts the target’s closure claim.

Disposition consequence: the design cannot bind until it chooses and specifies the land step. Either the automation lands the lifecycle-only change under an explicit policy/authority rule, or a durable owner/auto-merge path carries the second PR through merge. Otherwise the acceptance statement must be weakened to “opens a lifecycle PR,” which does not relieve P1.

## blocks-the-design — “criteria a merge genuinely establishes” has no closed decision procedure

Evidence: `packages/core/src/scope/acceptance-evidence.ts:193-267` recognizes only the four strict axes and returns suitable for every evidence kind when `requiredAxes.length === 0`; it rejects `merge`/`review` only when a strict axis was inferred. A merge commit and the delivery-ancestry proof in `packages/core/src/swarm/finalize-cohort.ts:592-610` prove that bytes landed. They do not prove an arbitrary non-strict acceptance sentence became true.

Failure mode: an auto-stamper must either infer semantics from criterion prose or stamp all criteria not recognized as smoke/UAT/deploy/observed-behavior. The latter falsely admits ordinary behavioral, documentation, migration, or configuration criteria whose wording does not trip the strict-axis regex; the former introduces an unbounded judgment path into a deterministic gate. The live evidence in comment 5433984468 shows the exact pressure failure: a relevant pointer was relabeled with a kind broad enough to pass.

Disposition consequence: define an authored, closed eligibility signal before any auto-stamp—for example an explicit merge-only requirement whose schema and gate semantics are tested—and stamp only that set. Unmarked or inferred criteria remain unattested. The existing strict-axis negative filter is not a positive proof that merge evidence is truthful.

## blocks-the-design — the proposed workflow cannot cover the named consumer repository

Evidence: the pinned tree contains repo-local workflows under `.github/workflows/`, but no consumer workflow template or workflow-deposit mechanism under `content/templates/` or `packages/core/src/deposit/`. `finalize-cohort` is a command executed in the checked-out project; a workflow installed in `deftai/directive` cannot observe or mutate `Shinran7/gh-stub` on that repository’s merge event.

Failure mode: the implementation can pass in this repository while the named Grok stop-at-PR-open fixture remains untouched in the consumer repository. External contributors to Directive are covered by a Directive workflow; external consumer repositories are not.

Disposition consequence: the target must name a distribution and upgrade surface for consumers (or an explicitly authorized cross-repository service) and test installation, permissions, and invocation in a consumer fixture. Without that, “works for ... UAT Tester 6 issue 6 / PR 7” is not implementable by the remedy sketched.

## sharpens-framing — use a merge event that already identifies the PR, and bound workflow authority

Evidence: `finalize-cohort --pr N` requires an exact PR number, while a delivery-branch `push` event describes a ref update and may contain no PR, one squash/rebase merge, or several merged PRs. The finalizer also performs `git push` and `gh pr create`, so the workflow needs repository write authority and operates on shared branch state.

Failure mode: “resolve the merged PR” becomes another heuristic that can miss or select the wrong PR; concurrent merge jobs can also race unless the branch/PR operation is idempotent and serialized. Broad write permissions enlarge the consequence of running newly merged repository code.

Disposition consequence: key the invocation from a closed-and-merged PR event (with base branch checked against the typed delivery branch), or specify a complete push-range-to-PR mapping. Document minimal token permissions, concurrency, retry/idempotency, and the behavior for multiple closing issues.

## Existing mechanisms and road not taken

`verify:pr-closeout-attestable` already reuses `evaluateAcceptanceEvidenceGate` and is wired into `pr:wait-mergeable-and-merge`; it is the sound place to refuse unattested criteria before a Deft-controlled merge. I rejected “auto-stamp every non-strict criterion after merge” even though it would make the sweep succeed, because the negative strict-axis filter is not positive evidence. I would change that verdict if the brief author must explicitly mark a criterion as merge-only and the runtime proves only merge ancestry for that closed class.

The useful thin slice is narrower: deterministically trigger the existing finalizer for already-attested briefs, make the lifecycle land path honest, and fail visibly on every remaining criterion. Automatic acceptance stamping should be a separate, explicitly typed capability rather than the condition needed to make post-merge cleanup appear complete.

Refutation charter, round 1, fresh critic. Pin-read `git show cb4c74369a888faabd01e7f8d3517b01ce25f2f1:`. Process-only; nothing implemented, nothing ingested.

## What survives

Part one of the target holds, and I could not break it.

`finalize-cohort` really is PR-scoped rather than cohort-scoped: `--pr <n>` fetches the merged PR, requires `base.ref` to equal the resolved delivery branch, requires `merge_commit_sha` ancestry against the refreshed remote tip, then maps structured closing refs to active briefs (`finalize-cohort.ts` `fetchPrDeliverySnapshot` / `fetchClosingIssues` / the closing-issue loop). Benign refs skip with a warning rather than aborting the sweep. A solo external PR was always a legal invocation. Nothing invokes it on merge. That gap is real and the fix is small.

The body's load-bearing source claim is also correct, and I re-derived it rather than taking the cite. The human-origin gate at `acceptance-evidence.ts:272` sits inside `parseDisposition`, not `parseEvidence`. `AcceptanceDispositionRecord` carries `provenance` and is checked with `isHumanOrigin`; `AcceptanceEvidenceRecord` has exactly `kind|pointer|recorded_at|recorded_by` and no provenance field at all. An automated actor genuinely may evidence a criterion and may not waive one.

What does not survive is the second half: that an automation can stamp `merge`-kind evidence **only for criteria a merge genuinely establishes**, and that the strict axes are **never** auto-stamped.

## 1. blocks-the-design — "only for criteria a merge genuinely establishes" has no mechanized proxy, and the nearest one is wrong on this issue's own criteria

**Evidence.** The only machine notion of "what kind can satisfy this criterion" is `inferRequiredStrictAxes` + `isEvidenceKindSuitable` (`acceptance-evidence.ts`). Suitability is consulted *only when the inferred axis set is non-empty*: `isEvidenceKindSuitable` returns `true` unconditionally for `requiredAxes.length === 0`. Axis inference is keyword regexes over `title`, `id`, and `narrative.Acceptance|Description|Test`.

I ported those regexes verbatim from the pinned source and ran them over this issue's own eight acceptance bullets. Five of eight infer **no** axis, so `kind: merge` is accepted for them by the gate:

- "Works for solo and external contributions, not only swarm cohorts" -> axes `[]`
- "A brief that cannot be fully attested automatically fails visibly and names what a human must supply" -> axes `[]`
- "A merge to the delivery branch automatically attempts the lifecycle move..." -> axes `[]`
- "The second-PR wrinkle above is resolved or explicitly accepted..." -> axes `[]`
- "`merge`-kind acceptance evidence is stamped only for criteria a merge genuinely establishes..." -> axes `[]`

**Failure mode.** The auto-invoke stamps `x-directive/evidence {kind: merge, pointer: <merge sha>}` on "Works for solo and external contributions, not only swarm cohorts". `evaluateAcceptanceEvidenceGate` returns `outcome: "evidence"`, `runTransition("complete")` advances the item, and the brief lands in `completed/` asserting that a merge commit establishes a behavioural claim about external contributions. The design's own safety valve -- "fails visibly and names what a human must supply" -- cannot fire here, because the gate does not refuse. It fails silently, in the direction of green, on exactly the criteria that need a reader.

This is comment 5433984468's finding reproduced structurally rather than behaviourally. That comment measured an agent under pressure choosing `test` for three markdown pointers, and concluded the kind field is the weak point. The remedy this issue proposes hands that same weak field to an unattended writer running at merge cadence, and keeps the same detector.

**Disposition consequence.** The second sentence of the refutation target cannot bind as written. "Genuinely establishes" is a judgement, and the only proxy in the tree answers it by keyword.

## 2. blocks-the-design — the same inference makes two of the recorded acceptance criteria unsatisfiable by the mechanism this issue specifies

I considered three remedies for finding 1 and took the third.

**Widen the axis taxonomy** so more criteria infer an axis. Rejected: it makes the keyword surface larger, not more reliable, and every new keyword is a new false positive of finding 2's shape.

**Kind-versus-pointer coherence**, as comment 5433984468 proposed. That check shipped, but only for one kind -- `uatPointerShapeError` guards `kind === "uat"` and nothing else. Extending it to `merge` is worth doing and I would take it, but it does not close finding 1: a merge-commit pointer is perfectly coherent with `kind: merge` on a criterion a merge does not establish. Coherence is necessary, not sufficient.

**Stamp only what the criterion explicitly declares.** `inferRequiredStrictAxes` already prefers explicit `requires` / `requiredEvidenceKind` / `acceptanceAxis` over prose, and falls back to keywords only when no explicit field is valid. Auto-stamp only criteria that carry an explicit declaration, and leave every inference-only criterion unattested and reported. That converts a judgement into a declaration made by whoever wrote the criterion, and it fails in the safe direction.

One taxonomy note if that route is taken: the explicit fields today accept only members of `STRICT_ACCEPTANCE_AXES` (`deploy`, `smoke`, `uat`, `observed_behavior`). `merge` is not among them, so `requires: merge` cannot be declared at this SHA. That is a small, bounded addition and it is the mechanism-shaped core of what part two actually needs.

## Steelman

The strongest case against me: keyword inference is the same rule `scope:complete` already applies to human stamps, so automating under it is no worse than the status quo and is more consistent -- humans forget, a machine never does, and 5433984468 is proof the human path already fails.

I take that seriously and it is half right. The difference is the reader. In 5433984468 an agent mis-stamped five items and another party caught it within hours by reading the stamps. An unattended stamper produces the same class of error at merge cadence, and the thing that caught it does not scale to every merge. Consistency in the direction of green is not a gain when the gate cannot refuse.

**What would flip my verdict on finding 1:** a characterization of the set "criteria a merge genuinely establishes" that does not route through prose inference. The explicit-declaration route above is one, and if it is adopted the finding is answered rather than argued down.

## Verdict

Part one of the refutation target survives intact and is worth building. Part two does not bind as written: findings 1, 2, and 3 are each sufficient on their own, and 3 defeats the leftover-active half regardless of how the evidence question is settled.

## Summary

The lifecycle move from `active/` to `completed/` cannot happen before a merge, but it is still performed **manually** afterwards. That manual step is what leaves orphaned briefs on master, and it is the one part of the sequence that does not need a human.

`task swarm:finalize-cohort` already exists and already does most of this. Automating its invocation on merge, and teaching it to stamp the evidence it can honestly produce, is a smaller change than any of the gates filed around this failure -- and closes more of the class.

## Why automation is the right layer

The window is structural and cannot be designed away. `scope:complete` refuses without delivery evidence: a merge commit that is an ancestor of the refreshed delivery ref, which by construction cannot exist before the merge. All three round-1 critics on the set critique verified this independently.

So the sequence is forced: merge, *then* complete. What is **not** forced is that a human performs the second step, or that an arbitrary amount of time passes between the two. Today the gap is bounded only by whether someone remembers.

Three occurrences in two days -- #3611, #3598, #3609 -- each an instance of nobody performing a step that a machine could have performed immediately.

## The incumbent is closer than it looks

Despite the name, `finalize-cohort` is **not** cohort-scoped:

```11:16:packages/core/src/swarm/finalize-cohort-cli.ts
export const FINALIZE_COHORT_USAGE = `Usage: task swarm:finalize-cohort -- [--pr <n>[,<n>...]] [options]

After cohort PRs merge, sweep story briefs active/ -> completed/ and open the lifecycle PR.

  --pr <n>[,<n>...]            Merged PR numbers (closing issues map to active stories)
```

It accepts arbitrary merged PR numbers and derives the stories from each PR's closing issues, so `--pr 3786` was always a legal invocation against the solo external PR that caused the most recent occurrence. Sibling `complete-cohort` (#1487) handles the sweep; #2225 shipped the post-merge flow.

Two things stop it closing the class today:

1. **It is opt-in.** Nothing invokes it on merge; someone has to remember, which is the same failure being automated away.
2. **It supplies delivery evidence but never acceptance evidence.** `completeCohort` routes through `runTransition`, which runs the acceptance gate unconditionally, so a brief with unattested items is refused no matter how it is invoked. This is why running it manually on #3609 would not have helped.

## Remedy sketch

**Part one -- invoke it automatically.** A workflow on master push resolves the merged PR and runs `finalize-cohort --pr <N>`. The window shrinks from "until someone notices" to "one CI run".

**Part two -- stamp the evidence a merge can honestly produce.** Give `finalizeCohort` the ability to record `merge`-kind acceptance evidence for criteria a merge actually establishes, with a truthful `recorded_by` naming the automation and a pointer to the merge commit.

This is legitimate rather than a loophole. The human-origin gate deliberately covers dispositions and not evidence:

```272:272:packages/core/src/scope/acceptance-evidence.ts
  // Reuse authz human-origin gate (#2944) so agent-self stamps cannot waive criteria.
```

An automated actor may not **waive** a criterion. Recording that something shipped, when it demonstrably shipped, is not a waiver.

## The constraint that must not be violated

**A merge cannot evidence every kind of criterion**, and automation that ignores this converts a lifecycle fix into a quality-gate bypass -- squarely #3156.

`merge` and `review` evidence cannot satisfy `smoke`, `uat`, `deploy`, or `observed_behavior` criteria; the #3240 taxonomy already encodes this. The automation must stamp only what the merge genuinely establishes and **leave the rest unattested**, failing loudly rather than defaulting to `test` because the field happens to accept any string.

A brief with criteria a merge cannot evidence should remain a human's job. That residual is exactly what the companion pre-merge gate is for.

## Known wrinkle

A successful `finalize-cohort` opens a **second** pull request carrying the lifecycle move. That PR must itself merge, so it recreates a smaller version of the same window. Worth deciding during design whether the lifecycle move can land without a second review cycle, or whether the shortened window is acceptable.

## Acceptance sketch

- [ ] A merge to the delivery branch automatically attempts the lifecycle move for the PR's closing issues
- [ ] `merge`-kind acceptance evidence is stamped only for criteria a merge genuinely establishes, with truthful `recorded_by` and a pointer to the merge commit
- [ ] Criteria requiring `smoke`, `uat`, `deploy`, or `observed_behavior` are **never** auto-stamped and are reported as remaining work
- [ ] A brief that cannot be fully attested automatically fails visibly and names what a human must supply
- [ ] Works for solo and external contributions, not only swarm cohorts
- [ ] Leftover-active after a resolvable merged issue is closed by that auto-invoke (named fixture: UAT Tester 6 issue #6 / PR #7 from #4715; Grok stop-at: pr-open leftover)
- [ ] The second-PR wrinkle above is resolved or explicitly accepted with a recorded rationale
- [ ] CHANGELOG `[Unreleased]` entry


## Leftover-active from #4715

Operator-deferred leftover-active P1 from #4715 (2026-09-18 design-critique Handoff). Detector and Envelope SLA leftover-owner already exist; the miss is that finalize-cohort is still opt-in, so a resolvable merged issue can leave its xBRIEF running in active/.

Named fixture: UAT Tester 6 issue #6 / PR #7 on consumer Shinran7/gh-stub (Grok Build, package 0.119.1). Envelope leftover: stop-at: pr-open leaves must not scope:complete; parent or Phase 6 swarm:finalize-cohort must. verify:orphan-active -- --issue N must exit 0 before DONE (#3429 / #4529).

This issue already claims solo and external PRs, not only swarm cohorts. Auto-invoke on merge must cover that Grok leftover path. Do not grow verify:orphan-active into a writer. Complementary closeout routes that are not this workflow stay on #3875.

## Out of scope

- Preventing an unattestable brief from merging in the first place (#3781). Complementary: this shortens the window, that one narrows what may enter it.
- Blast radius while an orphan exists (#3790).
- Changing the delivery-evidence requirement itself (#3041). Verified as genuinely structural; not this issue's target.

## Provenance

Filed on the round-1 set critique of #3781 / #3783 / #3790 (synthesis 5433848104), where all three critics independently identified post-merge automation as the missing remedy and the highest-value one. The `finalize-cohort` scoping and the acceptance-gate routing were verified against source by two critics and re-checked by the parent at `e2b62217`.

Refs #2225, #1487, #3781, #3790, #3240, #3041, #3156, #3609, #3598, #3611, #4715, #4529, #3429, #3875.

## Also reported

#4715 is the same stuck-active brief, closed as a duplicate of this issue. It is UAT Tester 6's field case (a merged issue left its xBRIEF in `active/`), a different person from the original audit filing. Two independent reports move this from High to Urgent.
